q: What does a transaction promise about several writes?
options: All of them happen, or none of them
They run faster
They run on separate servers
They can be undone any time later
why: A transaction turns several writes into one.

q: An error happens in the middle of a transaction. You then run COMMIT. What happens?
options: The steps before the error are saved
The transaction is already aborted, so COMMIT rolls everything back
Only the failed step is undone
Postgres asks you to confirm
why: An error aborts the whole transaction.

q: What does the D in ACID (durability) mean?
options: Data is deleted after a day
Data is stored twice in memory
After COMMIT, the data survives a crash, because the log is already on disk
Data is encrypted on disk
why: After a crash, Postgres replays the log: committed work stays, unfinished work goes.

q: Your code sends an email inside a transaction, and then the transaction rolls back. What went wrong?
options: Nothing, the email is recalled automatically
The email is sent again at the next commit
Postgres blocks all emails
The email was already sent. A rollback cannot undo the outside world
why: Write an outbox row inside the transaction, and send after the commit.

q: In Node with a `pg` pool, you run BEGIN, an UPDATE and COMMIT with `pool.query` three times. What is wrong?
options: Each call may use a different connection, so they are not one transaction. Use one client for all steps
Nothing, pool.query keeps the transaction open
COMMIT must be written in lower case
The pool must have only one connection
why: BEGIN, every step and COMMIT must go through the same client. Always release it in finally.
